I am 68, been farming these 8 mu since I was a boy helping my father. My wife helps me, but our son works in the city now so it is mostly me in the field. I will plant wheat this autumn and maize next summer — same as every year. This land has grown wheat and maize my whole life.

For wheat, I buy the improved seed from the same dealer in town. The varieties they sell now are good — shorter straw, do not fall down in wind. I will plant after October 8 when the soil cools. Before planting, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, 50 jin, I mean 50 kg. That gives the seed a good start. In spring when the wheat greens up and starts to stand tall, I put on urea, maybe half a bag per mu, 20-25 kg. My neighbor Old Zhang puts more, but I think that is wasteful. I water four times: once after planting if it is dry, once in March when it turns green, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. Wheat needs water or the grain stays empty.

For maize after wheat harvest in June, I do not plow — I just use the no-till planter, drop the seed right into the wheat stubble. Saves time and diesel. I use hybrid seed, everyone does now, the old kind gives poor yield. I put compound fertilizer in the row when planting, about one bag per mu. When the maize is knee-high I sidedress urea, maybe 30 kg per mu — maize eats more nitrogen than wheat, I learned this long ago. Maize I only water once or twice, depends on the rain. Hebei summer usually has enough rain but not always.

Pesticide — wheat I spray twice, once for aphids in spring, once for the disease on the head. Maize I spray once for the borer, sometimes twice if bugs are bad. I do not spray too much, the chemicals cost money.

Last year wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu, maize around 550. I expect about the same. Weather decides more than anything.
